name: France
summary: France is easier for vegans than its butter-and-cheese reputation suggests. Bakery bread, Provençal vegetable dishes and Nice's chickpea socca are vegan by tradition, and Paris has a large fully vegan restaurant scene. Outside cities, expect to ask for dishes without butter, cream or lardons.
phrase: Je suis végane. Je ne mange ni viande, ni poisson, ni œufs, ni produits laitiers, ni beurre, ni miel.
watch: Butter (beurre) in vegetables and sauces
Cream (crème) in soups
Lardons (bacon pieces) in salads and quiches
Meat or chicken stock (bouillon) in soups

name: Spain
summary: Spain's tapas culture includes many dishes that are vegan by tradition: tomato bread, Padrón peppers, chickpeas with spinach and cold gazpacho. The main risks are small pieces of ham (jamón) added for flavour, fish stock, and egg-based aioli.
phrase: Soy vegano (vegana). No como carne, pescado, huevos, lácteos ni miel. ¿Este plato lleva jamón o caldo de pescado?
watch: Ham pieces (jamón) added to vegetables and beans
Fish or chicken stock (caldo) in rice and soups
Egg in aioli (alioli)
Tuna (atún) in salads

dishes.name: Vegetable paella

name: the United States
summary: The United States has some of the world's strongest vegan restaurant scenes, led by Portland, Los Angeles, New York and Austin. Regional comfort food is harder: Southern greens, beans and refried beans are often cooked with pork, lard or chicken stock.
first_dish: A bean burrito in California, ordered without cheese or sour cream
phrase: I'm vegan: no meat, fish, eggs, dairy or honey. Is this cooked in butter, lard or chicken stock?
watch: Ham hock or bacon in collard greens and beans
Lard in refried beans and tortillas
Chicken stock in rice and soups
Butter on grilled vegetables and bread

dishes.name: Bean burrito
dishes.note: Ask for no cheese or sour cream and beans without lard.

dishes.name: Succotash

dishes.name: Three-bean chili

dishes.name: Peanut butter and jelly sandwich
dishes.note: Usually vegan; some bread contains milk or honey.

name: Italy
summary: Italy's peasant cooking (cucina povera) is full of dishes that are vegan by tradition: pizza marinara, pasta with tomato, bean soups and Sicilian chickpea fritters. Watch for Parmesan grated on top, anchovies in sauces, and fresh egg pasta.
phrase: Sono vegano (vegana). Non mangio carne, pesce, uova, latticini né miele. Senza parmigiano, per favore.
watch: Parmesan (parmigiano) grated on pasta and soups
Anchovies (acciughe) in sauces
Fresh egg pasta (pasta all'uovo)
Butter (burro) in northern dishes and risotto

name: Turkey
summary: Turkey (Türkiye) has a whole family of olive-oil vegetable dishes (zeytinyağlılar), traditionally served cold and made without meat. Lentil soup, stuffed vine leaves and the modern meat-free çiğ köfte are widely available. Butter and yogurt are the main things to ask about.

phrase: Veganım. Et, balık, yumurta, süt ürünleri ve bal yemiyorum. Tereyağı veya yoğurt var mı?
watch: Butter (tereyağı) poured over soups and rice
Yogurt (yoğurt) served on top

dishes.name: Sesame bread ring

name: Mexico
summary: Mexican food is built on corn, beans, chillies and vegetables, so many dishes are close to vegan. The catch is lard (manteca), used in beans, tortillas and tamales, plus cheese and cream on top. Learning to ask "sin manteca, sin queso, sin crema" opens up most menus.
phrase: Soy vegano (vegana). No como carne, pescado, huevo, lácteos ni miel. ¿Lo pueden hacer sin manteca, sin queso y sin crema?
watch: Lard (manteca) in beans, tortillas and tamales
Cheese (queso) and cream (crema) on top
Chicken stock (caldo de pollo) in rice
Mayonnaise on street corn

dishes.name: Cactus tacos
dishes.note: Grilled cactus paddles; ask for no cheese.

dishes.name: Guacamole

dishes.name: Beans

dishes.name: Street corn in a cup

dishes.name: Oaxacan tlayuda

dishes.name: Green chilli tamales
dishes.note: The dough is usually made with lard; vegan versions exist.

name: the United Kingdom
summary: The United Kingdom is one of the easiest countries to travel vegan. London and Bristol lead global vegan rankings, supermarkets label vegan products clearly, and pubs now commonly offer a vegan Sunday roast. Traditional fish-and-chip shops are the main thing to check.
first_dish: A vegan Sunday roast in a pub
phrase: I'm vegan: no meat, fish, eggs, dairy or honey. Are the chips fried in beef dripping?
watch: Beef dripping used to fry chips in some chip shops
Butter on vegetables and in mash
Worcestershire sauce (contains anchovies)
Egg and milk in Yorkshire puddings

dishes.name: Baked beans on toast

dishes.name: Vegan Sunday roast

dishes.name: Chickpea curry

dishes.name: Mushy peas
dishes.note: Marrowfat peas; check for butter.

name: Germany
summary: Germany, and Berlin above all, is one of the most vegan-friendly places in Europe, with vegan bakeries, supermarkets and döner shops. Traditional food is meat-heavy, but pretzels, potato salad and red cabbage can be vegan if you ask about bacon, lard and stock.
phrase: Ich bin vegan. Ich esse kein Fleisch, keinen Fisch, keine Eier, keine Milchprodukte und keinen Honig. Ist da Speck, Schmalz oder Brühe drin?
watch: Bacon (Speck) in potatoes and salads
Lard (Schmalz) in red cabbage and spreads
Meat stock (Brühe) in potato salad and soups
Egg in spätzle and noodles

dishes.name: Vegan döner

dishes.name: Fried potatoes

name: Japan
summary: Japan is beautiful for vegans who plan ahead and tricky for those who don't. Buddhist temple cuisine (shojin ryori) is fully plant-based, but dashi, a stock usually made from bonito fish, is in most soups, sauces and noodle broths.
first_dish: Shojin ryori at a temple in Kyoto or Koyasan
phrase: 私はヴィーガンです。肉、魚、卵、乳製品、はちみつを食べません。かつおだしも食べられません。
phrase_roman: Watashi wa bīgan desu. Niku, sakana, tamago, nyūseihin, hachimitsu o tabemasen. Katsuo dashi mo taberaremasen.
watch: Dashi (fish stock) in miso soup, noodle broth and sauces

name: Greece
summary: Greek Orthodox fasting has created a large tradition of food that is vegan by design, called nistisima (fasting food). Bean soups, stuffed vegetables, yellow split-pea purée and wild greens are on most taverna menus. Feta and yogurt are added by default, so ask.
